title: Why God’s Design Feels Slow… But Saves Your Soul
paragraphs:
Why God’s Design Feels Slow… But Saves Your Soul
The hidden war between instant pleasure and eternal purpose—and why choosing God will cost you everything… before it gives you everything.
There’s a moment no one talks about.

It’s not when you’re strong.
Not when you’re worshipping.
Not when you feel close to God.
It’s that quiet, almost invisible moment… when you’re tired… alone… scrolling… tempted… hurting… and something inside you whispers:
“Just this once.”

And suddenly, eternity feels distant…
and pleasure feels urgent.
That’s where the real war begins.

Not in church.
Not in public.
But in the unseen spaces where your soul negotiates with your flesh.
The Bible never pretended this would be easy. In fact, it exposes this tension with uncomfortable honesty. In the original Greek of the New Testament, James writes:
“Each person is tempted when he is dragged away and enticed by his own desire.”

That word “ἐξελκόμενος” (exelkomenos)… dragged away… like prey being pulled from safety.
And “δελεαζόμενος” (deleazomenos)… baited… like a fish lured by something that looks good but hides a hook.
That’s instant pleasure.
It never announces the cost upfront.
It just whispers… “this will feel good.”
And for a moment… it does.
But what it doesn’t tell you… is what it takes from you.

Your clarity.
Your peace.
Your identity.
Your intimacy with God.
Sin is not just breaking a rule. It’s stepping outside of design.

Because God didn’t give commands to control you…
He gave design to protect you.
From the very beginning, in the Hebrew of Genesis, we see this intentional design:
“וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים כִּי־טוֹב” (Genesis 1:31)

“Vayar Elohim ki-tov.”
“And God saw that it was good.”

Not random.
Not restrictive.
Good.
God’s design is not punishment… it’s alignment.

But instant pleasure doesn’t feel like rebellion in the moment…
it feels like relief.

Relief from stress.
Relief from loneliness.
Relief from pressure.
Relief from pain.
And that’s why it’s so dangerous.
Because it offers comfort… without covenant.
It gives you the feeling… without the foundation.
And slowly… quietly… it begins to rewrite who you are.
Paul exposes this internal conflict in a way that feels painfully real:
“ὃ γὰρ θέλω τοῦτο οὐ πράσσω, ἀλλ’ ὃ μισῶ τοῦτο ποιῶ.” (Romans 7:15)
“For what I want to do, I do not do… but what I hate, I do.”

If you’ve ever felt that contradiction inside you…
you’re not alone.
You’re human.
But you’re also being called higher.

Because God’s design doesn’t just deal with behavior…
it transforms desire.

Instant pleasure asks: “What do I feel right now?”
God’s design asks: “Who are you becoming?”
And that question changes everything.

Because the truth is…
every small choice is shaping a future version of you.

The one who keeps giving in…
or the one who learns to surrender.

Jesus didn’t come just to forgive sin.
He came to restore design.
In the Aramaic language He spoke, the word for sin is deeply connected to the idea of missing the mark—falling short of intended purpose.
And yet… He didn’t reject the broken.
He rewrote them.
The woman caught in adultery—exposed, ashamed, guilty—should have been defined by her scandal.
But Jesus looked at her… not through her failure… but through her future.
“Neither do I condemn you… go, and sin no more.” (John 8:11)

Grace didn’t excuse her sin.
Grace gave her a new direction.
That’s what makes God’s design better than instant pleasure.

Pleasure says: “Stay as you are… just feel better.”
Jesus says: “Come as you are… but I won’t leave you there.”
And that’s where it gets real.
Because choosing God’s design will cost you something.

It will cost you moments of temporary satisfaction.
It will cost you habits you’ve grown comfortable with.
It will cost you versions of yourself you’ve outgrown.
But what it gives you in return…
is freedom that doesn’t expire.
Peace that doesn’t depend on circumstances.
Identity that isn’t fragile.

And a relationship with God that isn’t built on performance…
but on transformation.
Be honest…
How many times has instant pleasure actually satisfied you long-term?
How many times did it leave you emptier… quieter… more distant?
Now ask yourself…

What if God isn’t withholding something from you…
but protecting something in you?

What if His design isn’t limiting your life…
but preserving your soul?
This isn’t about being perfect.
It’s about being honest.
Because some of you reading this… you’re tired.

Tired of the cycle.
Tired of the guilt.
Tired of pretending you’re okay.
And this moment… right now…
is an invitation.
Not to shame.
But to surrender.
Be real. Someone else needs to see your honesty and realize they’re not alone.
And don’t keep this to yourself.
Because comfort never saved a soul.
Jesus did.

And if you truly want to glorify God…
then don’t just receive truth—help it reach others.
Not as a transaction… but as participation in spreading the Gospel in a world drowning in distractions.
And beyond that…
If your spirit has been hungry… this is where you feed it.
Because following Jesus isn’t about occasional inspiration…
It’s about daily transformation.
And one day… you will look back and realize…

The things you thought you were losing…
were actually the chains God was breaking.
